headline: Montgomery flags ARB FY26 result materially better than feared, with strong 2H margin recovery driving relief rally and constructive FY27 outlook.
reasoning: ARB's FY26 result beat consensus expectations, with 2H26 PBT of $60.7 million coming in 5.2 per cent ahead of the $57.7 million consensus estimate and above even management's own guidance for a modest improvement over 1H26. The margin recovery was driven by two strategic price increases during FY26 and an easing of the AUD/THB exchange rate, rather than inventory adjustments. Currency hedges secured earlier in 2H at favourable rates could provide an FX tailwind into 2H27. Vehicle supply constraints, particularly around Toyota models, are expected to ease into 1H27, supporting the Australian aftermarket and OEM channel recovery. Export trends are broadly positive, with UK registrations recovering, Europe resilient, and new growth initiatives in China and South Africa. FY27 gross margins are expected to roughly align with FY26 full-year averages, and the combination of a 10–15 per cent uplift in engineering spend and improving operational capacity positions ARB well for the next leg of growth.
quote: ARB's FY26 financial result came in materially better than market fears, sparked by a strong second-half (2H26) margin recovery. While top-line sales performance remained somewhat subdued across the year, expanding profit margins comfortably offset the top-line softness. Profit Before Tax (PBT) for 2H26 landed at $60.7 million. This beat management's prior guidance for a modest improvement over 1H26 ($58.0 million) and tracked close to 2H25 ($63.0 million). Crucially, consensus expected 2H26 PBT of $57.7 million (with some buy-side estimates as low as $55.7 million), translating into a 5.2 per cent beat versus consensus. Given the weak share price performance leading up to the announcement and elevated short interest, today's combination of an earnings beat and a constructive outlook drove a sharp relief rally in the stock.
episode_title: ARB’s FY26 – A look under the hood

headline: Cooper Investors added ARB Corporation during the March/April Covid downturn, seeing it as a global compounding brand with strong recovery momentum
reasoning: ARB designs, manufactures, and sells 4x4 accessories globally and has compounded sales at 11% p.a. and EBITDA at 15% p.a. over 25 years. The pandemic initially disrupted the business but has since become a tailwind, as consumers redirect spending from international travel into outdoor/travel-related products. The order book recovered strongly in June and July (both record months), and Q1 FY2021 sales grew 17.7% versus the prior year, driven by export market growth. ARB is family/founder-led, has a net cash balance sheet, and Cooper Investors sees latent value in continuing export market expansion and OEM relationships.
quote: ARB is a compounding stock (growth subset of value) as we believe the company is well positioned to further monetize its IP and brand globally. Over the last 25 years, ARB has grown sales at a compound rate of 11% p.a. and EBITDA at 15% p.a. ARB sits in our Family-linked and Founder-led management category, having been led by Anthony, Andrew and Roger Brown since inception. As the global response to the pandemic stabilised, ARB's order book recovered strongly in June and July, both record months for the company. In some ways, the pandemic has now become a tailwind for ARB, with many consumers unable to spend on international travel and other discretionary items, spending has diverted for example into products related to travel/holidays. Therefore, even despite challenges still in Australia with Victoria in stage 4 lockdown, ARB recently reported a strong Q1 2021 sales growth of 17.7% (versus Q1 2020), underpinned by export market growth.

headline: Glenmore bullish on ARB Corporation after record sales months in June and July, with domestic travel tailwind supporting demand
reasoning: ARB's FY20 result showed revenue up 4.8% and NPAT up 0.3%, which Glenmore viewed as excellent given COVID headwinds and 28 consecutive months of declining Australian new vehicle market. Sales recovered strongly from April lows to consecutive record months in June and July. ARB deliberately de-stocked during March-April in anticipation of a prolonged downturn, creating short-term delivery issues that should resolve over 6-12 months. With international travel restricted, domestic travel should be a clear beneficiary once it reopens, driving demand for ARB's 4WD accessories range. Glenmore views ARB as one of the best-performing companies on the ASX over 20 years due to high-quality products and capable management.
quote: We viewed ARB's FY20 result, where revenue was up +4.8%, and NPAT up 0.3%, as an excellent outcome given the headwinds of Corona Virus and a very weak Australian new vehicle market (which has now declined 28 consecutive months). Unsurprisingly, sales for ARB were down materially in April-May, however pleasingly sales orders recovered strongly in May, resulting in consecutive record sales months in June and July. In addition, given the restrictions on international travel for the foreseeable future, domestic travel should be a clear beneficiary (once that re opens), which in turn should be very positive for demand ARB's range of products.

headline: Salt runs short in ARB Corporation on valuation and slowing Australian car sales headwinds
reasoning: ARB appeared as a contributor this month with the short down 8%. Goodson acknowledges it is a good business but could not justify a forward PE of over 33x at its peak. Australian car sales are slowing and rising petrol prices are expected to crimp demand in ARB's key gas-guzzling 4x4 segments. Salt sees the risk/reward as skewed to the downside.
quote: The second largest contributor was a large short in the bumper bar maker, ARB Corporation (ARB, -8%) which appeared on the opposite side of the ledger last month. It is a good little company, but it was beyond us as to what attributes drove it to a forward PE of over 33x at its peak. While Australians do have a love affair with their 4x4's, we see risks as skewed to the downside as Australian car sales slow and rising petrol prices may crimp sales in their key gas-guzzling segments.
